How Bridges Carry Weight

By Ada Lovelace

A bridge works by moving load from the deck into its supports. Every beam, cable and arch has a single job: to turn a vertical force into a force the ground can absorb, and to do it without bending further than the material allows.

Three basic forms

Engineers usually sort bridges into beams, arches and suspension designs. Read the full classification for the details, because each form spreads compression and tension in a different pattern across the span.

  • Beam bridges rely on bending strength
  • Arch bridges convert load into compression
  • Suspension bridges hang the deck from cables

Whatever the form, the designer has to account for wind, temperature, traffic and the slow settling of the foundations, since a structure that is perfect on the day it opens can still fail decades later if one of those loads was underestimated.
